articles.title: What Is LLVM?
articles.excerpt: When you look into how Rust is compiled, the name LLVM comes up. Here, I will compare it with Clang and GCC, familiar from C and C++, to clarify LLVM's role and see what rustc delegates to LLVM. LLVM…
articles.body: When you look into how Rust is compiled, the name LLVM comes up. Here, I will compare it with Clang and GCC, familiar from C and C++, to clarify LLVM's role and see what rustc delegates to LLVM . LLVM is infrastructure for building compilers LLVM is not the name of a programming language. It is a collection of reusable components and technologies for building compilers and related tools. See the official LLVM overview . The name LLVM can refer to the entire project or to its optimization and code generation infrastructure. When we say that Rust compilation "passes code to LLVM," we mainly mean the latter. That includes tasks such as transforming a calculation into a more efficient form and selecting instructions for ARM64 or x86-64.

articles.title: The Shift to Local LLMs: Replacing Cloud APIs with Gemma 3 in Developer Workflows
articles.excerpt: Originally published on tamiz.pro. For the past five years, the standard pattern for integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into applications has been straightforward: call a cloud API, pay per toke…
articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . For the past five years, the standard pattern for integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into applications has been straightforward: call a cloud API, pay per token, and accept the latency and privacy trade-offs. However, the release of highly optimized, small-parameter models like Google's Gemma 3 has disrupted this status quo. Developers are increasingly moving inference logic to the edge, specifically onto local hardware, to gain sub-second response times, eliminate data privacy concerns, and drastically reduce operational costs. This shift is not just about "running LLMs on your laptop"; it represents a fundamental architectural change in how modern software systems handle generative AI.

articles.title: MySQL max_user_connections Error on Shared Hosting: Fix
articles.excerpt: Most people who hit a MySQL connection limit ask the hosting company to raise the limit before they check why connections stay open. The max_user_connections error means one database user has reached…
articles.body: Most people who hit a MySQL connection limit ask the hosting company to raise the limit before they check why connections stay open. The max_user_connections error means one database user has reached the number of simultaneous connections it is allowed. The site can run fine for hours, then fail during busy traffic or right after a Laravel deployment. Quick answer: MySQL error 1203 means a database user has reached the server's per-user connection limit. On shared hosting that limit is often 25 concurrent connections. Run SHOW PROCESSLIST as that user to see idle (Sleep) sessions, stop overlapping Laravel queue workers, turn off persistent connections you don't need, and fix slow queries. Ask for a higher limit only after that.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks
articles.excerpt: The fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was one giant gimmick: shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.
articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

articles.body: The spooky season is officially here! Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs. In return, we have imprinted our myths, stories and perceptions upon it, seeing monsters and mythology in the twinkling lights of the stars and assigning sinister aspects to innocent cosmic objects. Many of these ghostly impressions and meanings have survived to the present day. Here are a few of our favorites.
